lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003e\u003cb\u003eMétodo n:
"

Neutral (covalent) method: metal electrons = group number (Cr 6, Fe 8, Ni 10, Rh 9…); each ligand contributes: CO, PR₃, alkene: 2 e⁻; Cl, H, alkyl: 1 e⁻; Cp (η⁵): 5 e⁻; 1 is added for each negative charge and 1 subtracted for each positive one. Example: Cr(CO)₆ = 6 + 6×2 = 18. In the 3D panel, each cube is an electron and its color indicates the origin (blue: metal; others: ligands).

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl \u003cb\u003ecatal:
"

Wilkinson's catalyst hydrogenates alkenes under mild conditions. Cycle: (1) loss of PPh₃ (16 → 14 e⁻); (2) oxidative addition of H₂ (Rh(I) → Rh(III), 14 → 16 e⁻); (3) alkene coordination (16 → 18 e⁻); (4) migratory insertion of the alkene into the Rh–H bond (18 → 16 e⁻, forms an alkyl); (5) reductive elimination of the alkane (Rh(III) → Rh(I), 16 → 14 e⁻). The catalyst is regenerated. The steps alternate 14, 16 and 18 e⁻.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl \u003cb\u003eferro:
"

Ferrocene, Fe(η⁵-C₅H₅)₂, has the iron between two cyclopentadienyl rings bound through the five carbons (hapticity η⁵). Neutral count: 8 (Fe) + 2 × 5 = 18 e⁻; in the ionic method: Fe²⁺ (d⁶) + 2 Cp⁻ (6 e⁻ each) = 6 + 12 = 18. Very stable, aromatic in the rings: it is a model of sandwich organometallic chemistry and undergoes electrophilic substitution reactions like benzene.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEn los \u003cb\u003ec:
"

In organometallic complexes the transition metal tends to surround itself with ligands until it completes 18 valence electrons: it fills its nine orbitals (5 d + 1 s + 3 p) with pairs, the “noble gas configuration”. It is the rule analogous to the octet rule. It is obeyed especially with strong-field and π-acceptor ligands (CO, phosphines, alkenes, Cp). There are reasonable exceptions: d⁸ square planar complexes are stable with 16 e⁻.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLos carbonilos binari:
"

Binary carbonyls are the classic example: Ni(CO)₄ (10 + 8 = 18, tetrahedral), Fe(CO)₅ (8 + 10 = 18, trigonal bipyramid), Cr(CO)₆ (6 + 12 = 18, octahedral). V(CO)₆ has 17 e⁻: it is a stable radical that is easily reduced to [V(CO)₆]⁻ (18 e⁻) or dimerizes. CO is a σ donor and a π acceptor (M→CO back-donation), which weakens the C≡O bond and strengthens M–C.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLos complejos \u003cb:
"

Square planar d⁸ complexes (Ir(I), Rh(I), Pt(II), Pd(II)) have 16 e⁻: the dx²−y² orbital is empty and there are free sites, so they are coordinatively unsaturated and very reactive. Examples: IrCl(CO)(PPh₃)₂ (Vaska), [PtCl₃(C₂H₄)]⁻ (Zeise), RhCl(PPh₃)₃ (Wilkinson). They can add H₂, alkenes, etc. and go to 18 e⁻ (octahedral d⁶).

"
